findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures.
findings.comment:
The facility has a TIME AS CONTROL policy in place for foods on the breakfast buffet, but the employee stated that they have been keeping some items to save on food cost. The following TCS food items were observed to be above 41F:

1. Waffle batter probed to be at 48F. Waffle batters are cold held using ice packs on the sides of the dispenser, which does not allow for proper cold holding below 41F. The employee stated that they have been putting the leftover waffle batters in the cooler to use for the next day. Cease doing this, as the waffle batters are not being properly cold held at below 41F and the package states to refrigerate the batter after it is made. 
2. There are two cold holding buffet lines that are cold held using ice below the containers. Cantaloupe probed to be at 47F and yogurt probed to be at 50F on one line. Cottage cheese probed to be at 48F, tomatoes probed to be at 47F, and watermelon probed to be at 50F on the second cold holding line. The employee stated that they had been saving the leftovers of these items. It was discussed to discard the leftovers after breakfast and to place less of the items out if wanting to save on food cost. 
3. There are two milk carafes, one containing 2% milk and the other containing almond milk. The employee stated that they place these back in the cooler after breakfast and the containers are emptied and cleaned every other day. Cease this practice. The milks should be discarded after breakfast and the containers should be cleaned daily. 

TIME AS CONTROL should be used for the breakfast buffet, as the facility does not have the equipment that allows for proper cold holding at 41F and below. The PIC stated that their policy is to use time as control. Ensure that all staff are educated on this and are being trained to discard items after breakfast. Ensure that TCS foods are being held at 41F and below.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Hot and Cold Holding. (A) Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control as specified under §3-501.19, and except as specified under (B) and in (C) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be maintained:(2) At 5°C (41°F) or less.

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container.
findings.comment: Illinois adopted the 2022 FDA Food Code which requires bulk/buffet items in establishments to have the major allergens listed on them. The items on the buffet need to have the major allergens listed in some form. This can be accomplished by a picture of the allergen outside of each one, a poster that lists the allergen next to each food item, or another form that clearly communicates the allergens container to the consumer.
findings.citation_text: 3-602.11(C) Food Labels. (C) Bulk FOOD that is available for CONSUMER self-dispensing shall be prominently labeled with the following information in plain view of the CONSUMER: (1) The manufacturer's or processor's label that was provided with the FOOD; or (2) A card, sign, or other method of notification that includes the information specified under Subparagraphs (B)(1), (2), (5) and (6) of this section.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present.
findings.comment: There were ants observed to be on the counter by the waffle maker, potato hot holding, and the microwave. The employee stated that they had been having an ant issue. Ensure that pest control is treating the facility for ants and that the counter is being frequently cleaned. A follow up is scheduled for 8/3/2026 to ensure that the ants have been eliminated from the facility.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.111 (A)(B) and (D) Controlling Pests. The PREMISES shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests shall be controlled to eliminate their presence on the PREMISES by: (A) Routinely inspecting incoming shipments of FOOD and supplies; (B) Routinely inspecting the PREMISES for evidence of pests; and (D) Eliminating harborage conditions.

Ensure that raw food items are never stored above RTE foods. Food should be protected from cross contamination during storage. 

 (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: The following food contact surfaces are observed to be in need of a cleaning: 

1. The containers for utensils in the drawers of the kitchen. 
2. The inside of the top of the ice machine is observed to have slight mold accumulation. 
3. The soda nozzles. 

Ensure that food contact surfaces are always clean to sight and touch. A follow up will be conducted on 11/15/2024 to ensure that these items have been cleaned and will regularly be cleaned. 

(A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-303.11: REPEAT- There was not a sanitizer bucket observed to be made at the beginning of the inspection. CORRECTED- A sanitizer bucket of Quaternary ammonium was made and tested at the correct concentration. Ensure that there is always a sanitizer bucket made during all hours of operation and food preparation to make sure that food contact surfaces are being properly cleaned and sanitized. 

(B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-302.13: There are not any equipment/supplies available to monitor the rinse temperature of the dish machine. Ensure that either temperature stickers or an irreversible registering thermometer are available. A follow up will be conducted on 11/15/2024 to ensure that one has been obtained. 

(B) In hot water mechanical WAREWASHING operations, an irreversible registering temperature indicator shall be provided and readily accessible for measuring the UTENSIL surface temperature.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-302.14: There are not any test strips available to measure the concentration of the Quaternary ammonium sanitizer. A follow up will be conducted on 11/15/2024 to ensure that Quat Sanitizer test strips have been obtained. It is important to always have test strips available to ensure that the sanitizer is at the correct concentration and food contact surfaces are being properly sanitized. 

A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean

NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.
